candidate.global_limitations: The analysis is strictly bounded to the starting position of the user role as represented in the earliest conversational turns, excluding downstream adjustments and rules made later in the dialogue.

records.fidelity_note: The user's starting position is not an outright rejection or acceptance of the software, but an inquiry driven by tension. They explicitly acknowledge in Turn 2 that informal peer pressure is already a feature of the status quo (e011), and therefore see the technological intervention as having dual possibilities—either mitigating public shame or systematically formalizing it (e014). This nuance is captured by preserving both the attraction and the counterpressure.
records.limitations: This assessment only covers the user's initial orientation in the first two turns. It does not incorporate concrete rules, committee plans, or technical failures that occurred during later implementation trials.
records.role_interpretation: The user seeks to resolve scheduling coordination issues while protecting cooperative values. They are attracted to the scheduling service's potential to improve coordination but lean conservative due to concerns that it might track cancellations, shift unstable burdens onto flexible workers, or formalize existing public pressures under a voluntary guise.

stance_components.object_interpretation: The scheduling service offers a promising prospect of better coordination for unpredictable shift demand.
The automated service could shift all scheduling uncertainty onto flexible members and quietly record who declines shifts.
Finding a way for the scheduling service to help the shop without measuring a member's cooperative commitment based on availability.
Whether the app-based software will successfully reduce existing public pressures or alternatively institutionalize and formalize them.

source_evidence.text: It also sounds like the kind of tool that calls something voluntary while quietly recording who always says yes.
We need coverage, but we are a cooperative; moving all uncertainty from the store onto the people with the most flexible lives would be a strange version of efficiency.
I want to know whether the service can help without turning availability into a measure of commitment.
One correction: the pressure is already here.
The software might reduce that pressure—or formalize it.
